jcr:content.jcr:description: Our story, our values, and our commitment to clients.
jcr:content.jcr:title: About Northstar Financial

subtitle.text: Fee-only advisors, founded in 2008, based in Philadelphia, serving 218 households in 31 states.

p1.text: Sarah Chen started Northstar in 2008 after ten years at a large wirehouse and one long year of watching good clients get bad advice because the advice paid well. The founding idea was that fiduciary should be the default, that conflicts of interest should be visible, and that fees should be simple enough to read on the back of a business card.

p2.text: Sixteen years later the firm is three advisors and two support staff. We work out of a small office on Market Street, meet most clients by video, and fly out a couple of times a year for the ones who prefer a table.

heading.headingText: What we try to hold to.

card.description: 100 percent employee-owned, no parent company, no sales quotas, no products to push. If someone else would be a better fit we will say so.
Plain-English explanations of fees, conflicts, and the reasoning behind every recommendation. If a client cannot explain it back to us we have not finished the conversation.
Average client tenure is 14 years. We make decisions with that in mind. Short-term thinking does not survive the first review.

text.text: Every advisor at Northstar holds the CFP designation and is a fiduciary for every recommendation we make. It is a legal standard, not a marketing line. We write it down in every engagement letter.

heading.headingText: What the first call looks like

text.text: The first call is 30 minutes, with one of the partners, by video or phone. We ask what brought you to us. You ask us whatever you want. We explain how we work. We will tell you plainly if we are not the right fit and recommend someone who might be.

jcr:content.jcr:description: A clear, collaborative path from first conversation to long-term partnership.
jcr:content.jcr:title: How We Work Together

subtitle.text: A working plan in about six weeks from the first conversation, then a long-term partnership that changes shape as your life does.

card.description: 30 minutes, no cost. We ask what brought you in today and what is keeping you up at night. You ask us anything you want, and we decide together whether it is a fit.
We send a short secure checklist of statements, tax returns, insurance policies, and estate documents. You upload what you have. We do the organizing from there.
Two meetings, three weeks apart. The first covers what we found and how we are thinking about the tradeoffs. The second is the written plan and our specific recommendations.
We run the plan with you. Opening accounts, moving assets, rebalancing portfolios, and coordinating with your CPA and attorney on anything that touches their world.
Quarterly portfolio updates, semi-annual check-ins, annual deep reviews. Plus unlimited calls when life does something you were not expecting.
A new baby, a job change, an inheritance, a market panic, or a big purchase that feels too big to make alone. You already have a team that knows the whole picture.

subtitle.text: Scenarios drawn from real engagements. Names and specifics have been changed to protect client privacy, but the moves are real and the numbers are close.

card.description: A dual-income couple in their mid-fifties assumed they would work until 67. When we modelled their actual spending we found they could stop at 64 by reshaping two 401(k) withdrawals and delaying Social Security by three years. The plan saved them 28 months.

titleElement.headingText: The Martins: Retiring Three Years Earlier

card.description: A founder selling her services firm for $4M came to us in the middle of the M&A negotiation. We coordinated with her CPA and attorney on the deal structure, ran tax projections on three exit scenarios, and built a post-sale withdrawal schedule before the wire cleared.

A client inherited $1.2M across a taxable brokerage, an inherited IRA, and a small trust. We consolidated the portfolio, built a ten-year RMD schedule for the inherited account, and set up a donor-advised fund to handle a year of unusually high income.
